items:
A work permit must be issued and qualified 
maintenance staff should carry the suitable safety category.
Safety fence (rope) with caution mark surrounding the work area.
Line isolation
Secondary injection test set
Ammeter, Voltmeter
Test lead

Make sure C.T secondary 
 circuit are shorted at the incoming terminal blocks before isolating the relay 
 current circuit for test
Obtain copy of relay setting from field maintenance file

Connect test leads between the current terminals (50 and 60) on the relay 
 Fig(1)
Connect test leads between the time delayed contacts (11 and 12) on the relay.
Connect test leads between the voltage terminals (-1and +2) on the relay
Increase the current slowly until the contacts close
Record this value on the test sheet

Record the time response of relay where the time will stop once the relay has 
 picked up
Compare the recorded values with setting values

Repeat the above test steps for other phases by putting the current terminals 
 for phase S (60 and 61) and phase T (50 and 70A)
Disconnect the test leads from the current terminals (50 and 60)
Disconnect the test leads between trip contact terminals (11 and 12)
Disconnect the test leads between trip voltage terminals (-1 and +2).

Check that the C.T and P.T secondary connections return to its normal position 
 as before the test

If any equipment associated with the relay has been isolated it should be 
 returned to the service

Protection | Technical Procedure
Introduction
This document out lines the testing procedure 
P1, which must performed on an annually bases as indicated by Y1 in the above 
title block
The TMAD relay is an electronic relay for three-phase diff. Protection with 
instantaneous operation. It is intended for the protection of rotating machines 
against internal faults. These faults must entail the interruption of generator 
excitation and the opening of load circuit
The first draft initiated by eng. Ayman Fathy Shita, teased eng. Badawy Abd El-Alim, 
eng. Hassan Ali El-Sherbeny & eng.Ayman Fathy Shita at 23 October 2003, revised 
by EDEPCo. quality control eng. Adel El-Nagare, accepted by General Director eng. Hamed 
El-Sayed Mansour and approved by eng. Uosry Salama Head sector of Power 
Stations.
Operation
The TMAD relay is a percentage diff. relay. Percentage "A" is defined for one 
phase as ratio of the difference between the source side current l1 and the 
line-side current l2 to half the sum of the two
A = 100 * (l1 -l2) / (l1 + l2) / 2
The currents l1 and l2 in the secondary of the current transformers source side 
and line side
Safety Precautions
A work permit must be issued and qualified 
maintenance staff should carry the suitable safety category.
Safety fence (rope) with caution mark surrounding the work area.
Line isolation
Tools and Equipment
Secondary injection test set
Ammeter, Voltmeter
Test lead
Work to be Carried Out
Make sure C.T secondary 
 circuit are shorted at the incoming terminal blocks before isolating the relay 
 current circuit for test
Obtain copy of relay setting from field maintenance file
Connect test leads between the current terminals (50 and 60) on the relay 
 Fig(1)
Connect test leads between the time delayed contacts (11 and 12) on the relay.
Connect test leads between the voltage terminals (-1and +2) on the relay
Increase the current slowly until the contacts close
Record this value on the test sheet
Record the time response of relay where the time will stop once the relay has 
 picked up
Compare the recorded values with setting values
Repeat the above test steps for other phases by putting the current terminals 
 for phase S (60 and 61) and phase T (50 and 70A)
Disconnect the test leads from the current terminals (50 and 60)
Disconnect the test leads between trip contact terminals (11 and 12)
Disconnect the test leads between trip voltage terminals (-1 and +2).
Check that the C.T and P.T secondary connections return to its normal position 
 as before the test
If any equipment associated with the relay has been isolated it should be 
 returned to the service
